candidates.teaser: Archaeologists found something inside an ancient Egyptian tomb that you could still eat today — and it's thousands of years old. 🍯
candidates.video_title: 3000-Year-Old Food Found in Egypt Still Edible
candidates.video_description: Deep inside Egyptian tombs, archaeologists discovered jars of honey that are over 3,000 years old — and still perfectly safe to eat. Honey's unique chemistry makes it virtually immortal. Could this be the world's most perfect food? #AncientEgypt #HoneyFacts #DidYouKnow #MindBlowing #FoodScience #ArchaeologyFacts #SurprisingFacts
candidates.script: What if I told you there's a food that literally never expires? Archaeologists digging inside ancient Egyptian tombs discovered honey that is over three thousand years old — and it was still perfectly edible. Honey's extremely low moisture content and naturally acidic pH create an environment where bacteria simply cannot survive. On top of that, bees add an enzyme that produces tiny amounts of hydrogen peroxide, acting as a built-in preservative. No other food on Earth can match this. So here's the question — if honey lasts forever, why does your grocery store jar have an expiration date?

candidates.teaser: There's a creature swimming in our oceans right now that is older than trees — yes, trees. 🦈
candidates.video_title: Sharks Existed Before Trees Even Appeared on Earth
candidates.video_description: Sharks have been roaming the oceans for over 450 million years, meaning they predate the existence of trees on land by nearly 90 million years. They survived every mass extinction on Earth. Does that make sharks the ultimate survivors? #SharkFacts #Prehistoric #Evolution #MarineBiology #NatureFacts #WildlifeScience #MindBlowing
candidates.script: Sharks are older than trees. Let that sink in. These creatures have been swimming in Earth's oceans for over four hundred and fifty million years. Trees, on the other hand, didn't appear on land until about three hundred and sixty million years ago. That means sharks existed for nearly ninety million years before the first tree ever grew. They survived the asteroid that wiped out the dinosaurs, they survived ice ages, volcanic eruptions, and five separate mass extinction events. Meanwhile, we nearly wiped them out in just a few decades of overfishing. So who's really the more dangerous species here?

candidates.teaser: Your body is hiding something inside it right now that can dissolve metal — and you had no idea. ⚗️
candidates.video_title: Your Stomach Acid Can Literally Dissolve Metal
candidates.video_description: The hydrochloric acid inside your stomach is so powerful it can dissolve razor blades and certain metals. Your stomach lining replaces itself every few days just to survive its own acid. How is your body doing this without destroying itself? #HumanBody #StomachAcid #BodyFacts #Science #Biology #MindBlowing #DidYouKnow
candidates.script: Right now, inside your body, there is an acid powerful enough to dissolve razor blades. Your stomach produces hydrochloric acid with a pH between one and two — that's strong enough to corrode certain metals. The reason it doesn't eat through your stomach is that your stomach lining produces a thick protective layer of mucus, constantly renewing itself every three to four days. The moment that protection breaks down, you get a stomach ulcer — essentially your stomach starting to digest itself. You are, quite literally, one thin layer of mucus away from self-destruction. Still feeling hungry?

candidates.topic: Oxford University older than Aztec Empire
candidates.teaser: One of the world's most famous universities was already ancient by the time a legendary empire was just getting started. 🏛️
candidates.video_title: Oxford University Is Older Than the Aztec Empire
candidates.video_description: Oxford University began teaching students around 1096 AD, while the Aztec Empire wasn't founded until 1428 AD — making Oxford over 300 years older. History isn't always what we imagine it to be. Which other facts have you been getting backwards? #OxfordUniversity #AztecEmpire #HistoryFacts #MindBlowing #DidYouKnow #AncientHistory #SurprisingHistory
candidates.script: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire — and most people have this completely backwards. Oxford started teaching students around 1096 AD. Scholars were walking its halls, debating philosophy and science, for over three hundred years before the Aztec Empire was even founded in 1428. By the time the Aztecs were building Tenochtitlan, Oxford already had centuries of academic tradition behind it. We tend to think of medieval Europe as primitive compared to ancient civilizations, but the timeline tells a very different story. What other historical facts do you think you have backwards?

candidates.topic: Wi-Fi uses same frequency as microwave
candidates.teaser: The device you use to heat your food and the signal streaming your videos are operating on the exact same frequency. 📡
candidates.video_title: Your Wi-Fi and Microwave Run on the Same Frequency
candidates.video_description: Your home Wi-Fi router and your microwave oven both operate at 2.4 gigahertz — the exact same frequency. That's why your internet slows down when someone uses the microwave nearby. Technology is stranger than we think. #WiFi #MicrowaveOven #TechFacts #Physics #DidYouKnow #EverydayScience #MindBlowing
candidates.script: Your Wi-Fi router and your microwave oven are running on the exact same frequency — 2.4 gigahertz. Microwaves heat food by vibrating water molecules at this frequency, and your Wi-Fi transmits data through the air at this same frequency. This is why your internet connection can actually slow down when someone turns on the microwave in the kitchen — they're literally competing for the same space in the electromagnetic spectrum. Engineers knew about this conflict when designing home networks and worked around it as best they could. So next time your video buffers, maybe check if someone's reheating leftovers. Does that change how you think about your kitchen?
